project_guidance.note: How to talk about the projects. This is framing, not extra facts — every claim must still come from the project entries themselves.

tiers.flagship: The three strongest, each for a different reason: QuickFix (distributed AI systems engineering), Community AI Platform (full-stack product with real users), Steel Surface Defect Detection (ML research with a paper under review).
tiers.substantial: Real, shipped applications that show breadth: SOEIT Student Achievement Portal, ArthaNova, 3D Interactive Portfolio.
tiers.supporting: Smaller focused builds that demonstrate specific fundamentals: Age & Gender Prediction, Combat Online Plagiarism, Sentiment Analysis Pipeline, Black Friday Sales Prediction.

project_guidance.answering_superlatives: There is no single 'best' project on record. When asked for the strongest/best project, present the three flagships and say what each one demonstrates, then pick the most relevant one for the role being hired for. If the role is unknown, ask. Do not silently default to whichever project has the loudest numbers.
project_guidance.honesty_note: Tier and 'best for' labels are an organising assessment of the evidence below, not claims Ritesh has made. Say so if asked how the ranking was decided.

projects.name: QuickFix — AI-Powered Customer Complaint Management System
projects.best_for: Backend engineering, AI/LLM systems, distributed architecture
projects.why_it_stands_out: The most architecturally ambitious build: an orchestrated system of 30+ specialised AI services with a 3-tier model fallback, sustaining 15,900+ requests a day at under 200ms.
projects.hardest_part: Making more than thirty specialised agents route correctly and answer consistently, while keeping every reply grounded in the company's real policy documents rather than guessed.
key_decisions: Many small specialised agents instead of one general model — the system reads a complaint and routes it to the right expert, like a well-run call centre.
RAG so the AI 'reads the manual' before it speaks, giving policy-backed answers rather than plausible-sounding ones.
A 3-tier fallback (Groq LLaMA 3.3 → Gemini 2.0 Flash → local TF-IDF) so the system degrades gracefully instead of going down when a provider fails.
projects.problem: Support teams are slow and inconsistent at resolving complex customer complaints across many policy edge-cases.
projects.what_was_built: A full-stack complaint resolution platform with an async pipeline of 30+ specialized AI services (Orchestrator, Classifier, Sentiment Analyzer, Priority Detector, RAG Engine). A RAG engine grounds answers in the company's actual policy documents so replies are policy-backed rather than guessed.
engineering_details: Sustains 15,900+ daily requests at <200ms response time.
3-tier LLM fallback chain: Groq LLaMA 3.3 → Gemini 2.0 Flash → local TF-IDF, so the system degrades gracefully instead of failing.
Google OAuth 2.0 + email OTP authentication, JWT-based role access control, Brevo SMTP notifications.
FastAPI backend orchestrates the agents; database stores every complaint and its history for conversational context.

projects.name: Community AI Platform
projects.status: Live in production at communityai.co.in, serving real users
projects.best_for: Full-stack product engineering, applied AI, social-impact products
projects.why_it_stands_out: The project with the clearest real-world impact: a live multilingual platform that puts 50+ government schemes within reach of people who would never find them otherwise.
projects.hardest_part: Designing the whole product around one question an ordinary user actually asks — 'what am I eligible for, and how do I get it?' — when the underlying information is scattered across dozens of sites, written in complex English and buried in PDFs.
key_decisions: Async FastAPI so a single service can serve many concurrent users on modest hosting.
SQLAlchemy models plus Pydantic validation so malformed or malicious input is rejected before it reaches the database, without writing raw SQL.
A multi-model pipeline (Groq → Gemini fallback) with source attribution, so answers can be traced back to where they came from.
A lightweight React frontend, because the target users are often on budget phones.
projects.problem: Government help exists, but people never find it — details are spread across dozens of sites, written in complex English, and buried inside PDFs. Underserved communities can't discover the resources meant for them.
projects.what_was_built: A multilingual platform providing access to 50+ government schemes, learning resources and job opportunities across India, with a context-aware AI chat assistant and deep-learning-driven recommendations that surface relevant opportunities from a user's profile.
engineering_details: Async FastAPI backend with SQLAlchemy models for users, schemes and chat history; Pydantic validates every request before it reaches the database.
JWT-based authentication for private pages.
Multi-model AI pipeline (Groq → Gemini fallback) for source-attributed Q&A.
Content ingestion via News and YouTube APIs.
Supports English, Hindi, Bengali, Telugu and Marathi.
Responsive React frontend designed to run well on low-end phones.

projects.name: Steel Surface Defect Detection (AMFF-CNN)
projects.status: Ongoing research at NIT Jamshedpur; paper under review at Discover Artificial Intelligence (Springer Nature)
projects.best_for: Machine learning, computer vision, research roles, edge deployment
projects.why_it_stands_out: The only project with peer-reviewed research behind it — an original architecture (AMFF-CNN) with measured results, 98.33% accuracy and 0.85 mAP, and a paper under review.
projects.hardest_part: Detecting defects that range from large blotches to hairline cracks with one model, while keeping it small enough to run on cheap hardware beside the production line rather than on a server.
key_decisions: MobileNetV2 as the backbone specifically because factories need models that run on small, cheap edge hardware next to the camera.
A Feature Pyramid Network plus attention-based multi-scale fusion so the model examines the image at several zoom levels and focuses on the regions that matter.
OpenCV preprocessing to standardise size, contrast and lighting across thousands of images, so the model always learns from consistent examples.
projects.role: ML Researcher — Machine Vision and Intelligence Lab, NIT Jamshedpur
projects.problem: Manual quality control on steel surfaces is slow, costly and inconsistent at spotting fine defects on a live production line.
projects.what_was_built: A lightweight defect detector combining a MobileNetV2 backbone, a Feature Pyramid Network and attention-based multi-scale feature fusion (the AMFF-CNN design), trained on the 6-class NEU-DET dataset for industrial quality control.
engineering_details: OpenCV preprocessing pipeline to standardize size, contrast and lighting across thousands of steel-surface images.
MobileNetV2 backbone chosen so the model runs on cheap edge hardware next to the camera, not only on servers.
FPN + attention-based multi-scale fusion so both large blotches and hairline cracks are detected.
Trained and validated in PyTorch.

projects.name: SOEIT Student Achievement Portal
projects.best_for: Full-stack engineering, role-based access control, product workflows
projects.why_it_stands_out: The clearest example of replacing a manual institutional process with software — three user roles, a verification workflow, and one-click ATS-compliant resume generation.
projects.hardest_part: Modelling one submission workflow that works for three different roles at once — students uploading, faculty verifying, admins managing — without the permissions leaking into each other.
key_decisions: Role-based access control as the organising principle rather than an afterthought.
Categorised, searchable, filterable records so users find things instead of scrolling spreadsheets.
Docker for consistent deployment; Google OAuth and Brevo for auth and notifications rather than rolling both by hand.
projects.problem: Student achievements are scattered across emails, spreadsheets and paperwork; students lose track of certificates and faculty spend hours verifying records.
projects.what_was_built: A full-stack academic platform with three roles (Student / Faculty / Admin) covering achievement submission and verification, certificate uploads, gamified leaderboards, bulk certificate export, and one-click ATS-compliant resume generation.
engineering_details: Role-based access control: students submit and track, faculty verify, admins manage users and records.
React 19 frontend, responsive across desktop and mobile.
Node.js/Express backend handling authentication, validation and database operations.
Categorized, searchable and filterable achievement records replacing manual paperwork.
Containerized with Docker; Google OAuth and Brevo API integrated.

projects.name: ArthaNova — Personal Finance Dashboard
projects.best_for: Frontend engineering, data visualisation, dashboard UX
projects.why_it_stands_out: A focused exercise in making numbers legible — turning raw financial data into charts and summaries a non-expert can read at a glance.
projects.hardest_part: Making financial data feel simple when most tools in the category overwhelm people with detail.
key_decisions: Reusable React components with responsive layouts and real-time updates as the user interacts.
A modular architecture designed so new financial features can be added without rework.
projects.problem: Most people know where they earn money but not where it goes; traditional finance tools feel overwhelming.
projects.what_was_built: An intuitive dashboard that turns financial data into simple charts, summaries and visual reports so users can understand spending and trends at a glance.
engineering_details: Reusable React components with responsive layouts and real-time updates.
Frontend talks to backend APIs to fetch and update financial data dynamically.
Modular, scalable architecture designed for adding new financial features.

projects.name: Age & Gender Prediction
projects.why_it_stands_out: Shows a trained model turned into something that runs live on a camera feed, not a result hidden inside a notebook.
projects.hardest_part: Doing detection and prediction fast enough per frame to feel instant, while coping with varied lighting and face angles.
key_decisions: Haarcascade for face detection first — classic and very fast — so the CNN only ever sees a cropped face.
Optimising the loop for the speed/accuracy trade-off rather than chasing benchmark numbers.
projects.what_was_learned: How to balance speed against accuracy, and how much work it takes to move a trained model from test data to something that runs smoothly for a real user.
projects.problem: Biometric and analytics systems need fast, accurate age and gender estimation from a live camera feed.
projects.what_was_built: A real-time deep-learning app that detects faces with a Haarcascade classifier and predicts age range and gender with a CNN, drawing results onto the live video stream.
engineering_details: Haarcascade face detection per video frame before prediction.
CNN built and trained in PyTorch on cropped faces.
Inference loop optimized so detection and prediction feel instant on a live feed.

projects.name: Combat Online Plagiarism with AI
projects.why_it_stands_out: Attacks a loophole rather than a task: catching reworded plagiarism that literal text-matching always misses.
projects.hardest_part: Judging similarity by meaning rather than wording, so swapping 'big' for 'large' no longer defeats the checker.
key_decisions: Transformer embeddings so two sentences that say the same thing in different words end up with similar vectors.
Cosine similarity to score how aligned two ideas are, with high-scoring pairs flagged for a human to review rather than auto-judged.
projects.what_was_learned: How modern AI represents language as numbers, and how a simple, well-chosen mathematical comparison on top of those numbers can solve a problem exact matching never could.
projects.problem: Exact-match plagiarism checkers miss paraphrased or reworded content — swapping a few synonyms defeats them.
projects.what_was_built: An NLP system that converts text into Transformer embeddings and flags likely plagiarism using cosine similarity between meanings rather than literal text matching.
engineering_details: Text converted to vector embeddings that capture meaning.
Cosine similarity scores how aligned two pieces of text are (0 = unrelated, 1 = essentially identical).
High-similarity pairs are flagged for human review.
impact: Catches paraphrased plagiarism that literal matching misses

projects.name: Sentiment Analysis Pipeline
projects.why_it_stands_out: Ends at a decision, not a score: interactive charts let a non-technical reader see sentiment trends instead of reading numbers.
projects.hardest_part: Turning a mountain of raw opinions into a story a decision-maker can act on in seconds.
key_decisions: VADER because it handles everyday language including slang and emojis with no heavy training required.
Plotly charts so anyone can hover and filter — pairing a fast scorer with strong visualisation rather than chasing a bigger model.
projects.problem: Teams need to read sentiment across large volumes of text quickly, and see it rather than just score it.
projects.what_was_built: An end-to-end sentiment scoring pipeline using VADER with dynamic Plotly visualizations for fast, readable results.
engineering_details: VADER handles everyday language including slang and emojis with no heavy training required.
Automated ingest → clean → score → organize flow for large batches.
Interactive Plotly charts let non-technical users hover and filter to see sentiment trends.

projects.name: Black Friday Sales Prediction
projects.best_for: Classical ML on tabular data, feature engineering
projects.why_it_stands_out: Answers a concrete money question — how much will this customer spend — and covers the full data-science workflow end to end.
projects.hardest_part: Turning messy real sales records into features a model can actually learn from.
key_decisions: Pandas feature engineering to convert raw records (age, product category, past purchases) into clear signals.
XGBoost and LightGBM because gradient boosting handles complex patterns in tabular data particularly well.
projects.what_was_learned: The full workflow — cleaning, feature engineering, modelling and evaluation — tied to a business question rather than a benchmark.
projects.problem: Retailers lose money on both overstock and stockouts; the fix is forecasting customer spend in advance.
projects.what_was_built: A prediction engine using XGBoost and LightGBM to forecast customer spending behavior from historical sales data.
engineering_details: Pandas-based cleaning and feature engineering from raw records (age, product category, past purchases).
Gradient-boosting models (XGBoost, LightGBM) chosen for strong performance on tabular data.
Full data-science workflow: cleaning, feature engineering, modelling, evaluation.

projects.name: 3D Interactive Portfolio (riteshkr.info)
projects.best_for: Frontend engineering, animation, 3D on the web
projects.why_it_stands_out: Demonstrates front-end skill on arrival instead of describing it — and now hosts this AI representative, which answers recruiter questions from a structured profile.
projects.hardest_part: Adding genuine 3D and heavy animation without making the page slow on an ordinary device.
key_decisions: React + Vite for component reuse and a highly optimised production build.
Tailwind for a consistent design system and the dark/light theme.
Framer Motion for entry animation, GSAP ScrollTrigger for scroll reveals, React Three Fiber for the 3D layer.
A FastAPI backend for the AI chat, with answers grounded strictly in a validated profile file.
projects.problem: A portfolio should demonstrate front-end skill on arrival, not just describe it — while still loading fast on any device.
projects.what_was_built: A React + Vite portfolio with Tailwind CSS theming (dark/light), Framer Motion and GSAP scroll animations, genuine 3D particle backgrounds via React Three Fiber, and an interactive skill explorer, plus this AI chat representative.
engineering_details: Component-driven React architecture built with Vite for optimised production bundles.
Tailwind CSS design system with a dark/light theme toggle.
Framer Motion for entry/modal animation, GSAP ScrollTrigger for scroll reveals.
React Three Fiber / Three.js for 3D visuals without hurting page performance.
